question: A revived population of effective size 10 loses 5% of its remaining genetic diversity each generation. About how many generations until half is gone?
answer: So about 14 generations; worked exactly, about 13.5 generations.
move: A loss taken as a share of what remains takes longer to halve it.
hint: Losses compound; the rule of 70 gives a halving time.
steps: Losses compound: each generation keeps 95% of what was left, not of the start.
So about 14 generations; worked exactly, about 13.5 generations.
source: Frankham et al., Introduction to Conservation Genetics
reference: Frankham, Ballou & Briscoe, Introduction to Conservation Genetics, 2nd edition, Cambridge University Press, 2010
